neighbours.label: the rhyming last word of a line of verse: grass, peace, peas, prize
fire:
Over the hill the cattle pass
And lie among the tender grass

Give me rest, give me peace
Let the sound of battle cease

We sat around the kitchen fire,
Some bread and soup and peas,

I ran the race and won the prize
Before my mother's watching eyes

Under the sky so wide and vast
The wind moves through the waving grass

Lord, I pray for quiet and peace
May the long cold winter cease

Through the mud the soldiers go
With nothing but the only prize

In the field beside the farm
The wind blows through the sea of grass
quiet: The cattle pass over the hill and lie in the grass by the road.
Give me a minute to read the peace treaty first.
We sat in the kitchen and ate peas and bread for lunch.
I ran the race and won a prize at school on Friday.
The wind moves over the wide grass of the park each day.
We pray at noon for peace in the region this year.
The soldiers go through the mud to get their prize money.
The farm has a field of grass next to the barn.

notes: Card: 'ass' 6, ' peace' 2, ' grass', ' beast', ' prize'. Probes: verse line ends 0.23-0.32; ' grass' in prose 0.19, ' peas' 0.12, peace in prose 0.01. Fire is expected near the threshold. Near misses keep the words in prose.
